title: AI-use policy record for one publishing entity

parent.description: id of the entity whose policy this one inherits, or null

platform.description: Where content is hosted. NOT the same as policy_owner — EMBO sits on Springer Nature Link but sets its own policy. Conflating them invents a false inheritance.

policy_owner.description: id of the entity that actually writes this policy

delegates_to_journal.description: true only where individual journals genuinely deviate. Verified true for OUP and CUP; false for every other publisher checked.

policy_architecture.description: The SHAPE of the policy object. Converging on per-activity grids during 2026 while the content diverges — record both.

url.description: null ONLY where the quote is held but the URL is not yet confirmed. Never construct a URL by pattern.

status.description: stale_but_live is the trap: still HTTP 200, still findable, no longer correct.

authoritative.description: Powers the 'cite this, not that' layer. Exactly one source per audience should be true.

fetch_method.description: 18 of 29 society URLs 403 to curl. COPE is Cloudflare-blocked entirely. The fetcher needs to know before it tries.

date_source.description: Most publishers date nothing. Where there is no stated date, the content hash IS the date.

adjudicated_sha256.description: Text-hash a human last signed off. diff.py compares against THIS, not against the previous fetch — otherwise an unadjudicated change is overwritten and lost on the next run, which is exactly how the closest precedent to this project froze.

note.description: Why this source is fetched the way it is — e.g. why an archive capture stands in for a live page.

axis.description: An activity key from schema/stm-activities.yml, or an extended-axis key.

permission.description: not_addressed is a real value, not a blank. It is the modal value across the corpus and the cell most likely to change first.

disclosure.description: Sherpa's vocabulary, adapted. Separates silence (not_addressed) from an explicit exemption (not_required).

disclosure_location.description: Wiley routes by purpose; Springer Nature is silent; Elsevier fixes one position. This field alone discriminates.

rationale.description: The GROUND of the rule, not its verdict. The ERC and DFG reach opposite conclusions from different principles; recording only the verdict loses that.

quote.description: Verbatim, short, attributed. Never paraphrase — paraphrase is where this resource would lose its only asset.

quote_provenance.description: raw_bytes = extracted from the fetched document. summariser_relayed = passed through a summarising fetch layer, so carries paraphrase risk. Different fabrication risk; nobody else distinguishes them.

evidence_role.description: supports (default): the quote establishes the verdict. documents_absence: the verdict is not_addressed and the quote shows what the entity says INSTEAD of addressing it. Without this, a silent cell carrying a quote reads as a contradiction and a reader cannot tell which is meant.

coherence.description: SUBSTANTIVE contradictions only: two live sources of this entity that give a reader conflicting instructions on the same question. Both sides must be quoted AND linked. Anything a publisher could rebut in one sentence belongs in metadata_inconsistency or nowhere.

metadata_inconsistency.description: Dating, tagging or versioning oddities. Real, and useful to a scraper — but NOT policy self-contradiction, and they must never be counted as such. Publicly labelling a stale HTML title tag a 'self-contradiction' is indefensible.
